scope: Exact first-mark residual order classification and matching-plus-isolate odd-order coefficient calculation; no claim of universal coverage.
structural_facts: Distinct marks in W are pairwise nonadjacent because all are neighbors of the deleted support in an ordinary tree.
Residual order 2k+1 requires a deletion union of size 2, hence i=1 and degree_H(w_1)=1.
Residual order 2k requires a deletion union of size 3: either i=1 and degree_H(w_1)=2, or i=2 and degree_H(w_2)=1 with the one earlier mark outside N_H[w_2].
Residual order at most 2k-1 has i_k(J) <= i_(k-1)(J) by the independent-set incidence count: k*i_k(J) <= (|V(J)|-k+1)*i_(k-1)(J) <= k*i_(k-1)(J).

matching_plus_isolate.graph: k disjoint edges and one isolated vertex
matching_plus_isolate.derivation: i_r = 2^r*binomial(k,r) + 2^(r-1)*binomial(k,r-1); subtract at r=k and r=k-1.

matching_m_plus_isolates.graph: m disjoint edges and L=2k+1-2m isolated vertices

limits: No realizability claim is made for the matching residual within a guarded T, H, W, and selector instance.
The order-2k residuals at this parent order delete three vertices and are not covered by the supplied first-shell two-vertex edge classification.
No universal boundary sign or global compensation inequality has been proved.
